hero.eyebrow: Haus Till E on the Moselle bend in Zell
hero.sub: In this listed Art Deco house full of history, five individual double rooms await you, each brimming with charm and character. Start the day with a delicious breakfast in our cosy breakfast room — before losing track of time in our wildly romantic garden.

text: Once upon a time, there was a castle owner with three daughters — and he bequeathed each of them a part of the Zell castle, built in the 16th century: to one the side wing, to another the main house, and for the third he had a new building erected, designed to blend harmoniously in style and appearance with the castle ensemble.

What sounds like a fairy tale is actually a true story from the 1920s in Zell. This is how the property came to be that is known and cherished today as Haus Till E. Our listed building dates from the Art Deco era and has been lovingly restored in the style typical of that period. Windows, doors, wooden floors and the staircase are all original, giving the house its unique flair.
In front of the house awaits a wildly romantic, idyllic garden. Over a bottle of wine, you can let your soul relax here and lose track of time, before diving back into the history of these walls.

accordion.title: Directions
accordion.content:
How do I get to Haus Till E?

Haus Till E is within walking distance of the Moselle, right in the heart of Zell's old town, at Schloßstraße 10. Coming from Bullay, you drive through the Zell-Merl district into Zell's old town. Other routes lead via the Zeller Berg and Grenderich (L199), through the Altlay valley (L194), or from Kappel via the B421. By train, you can reach us via the Bullay eco-station — from there, a bus takes you about 3 km to the Lindenplatz stop, just a short walk from Haus Till E. The nearest airport is Frankfurt-Hahn (approx. 20 km). Whether from the train station or the airport: just let us know — we're happy to pick you up by car! (for a small contribution towards costs)

accordion.title: Address
accordion.content:
Where exactly is Haus Till E located?

Haus Till E is located at Schloßstraße 10, 56856 Zell (Mosel) — right at the foot of the steep vineyard „Zeller Schwarze Katz“, just a few minutes' walk from the Moselle promenade and the old town.

accordion.title: Prices
accordion.content:
How much does a night in a double room cost?

€110–140 per night (depending on weekday and availability)

Is breakfast included in the price?

Yes, breakfast is included in the price for the double room (€110–140).

accordion.title: Parking
accordion.content:
Is there free parking nearby?

Numerous free parking spaces are available along the Moselle riverside. You can park directly on Schloßstraße with a parking ticket — for loading and unloading your luggage, the free 30-minute ticket is usually enough.

accordion.title: Pets
accordion.content:
Are dogs allowed at Haus Till E?

We both love dogs dearly — but over the years we've had some experiences that led us to rethink. For this reason, bringing dogs to Haus Till E is currently not possible. Thank you for your understanding.

accordion.title: Limitations
accordion.content:
Is there a lift?

Haus Till E is a listed building from the 1920s with no lift — the rooms are only accessible via the stairs.

Is smoking allowed inside?

Smoking is not permitted inside the house, including on the balconies; however, you are welcome to smoke in our garden at any time.

accordion.title: Bicycles
accordion.content:
Can I safely store and charge my bike?

You can safely park and charge your regular or electric bicycles in our outbuilding.

Can I rent a bike locally?

Our guests are especially happy with the bike rental services from Wanderland (Balduinstraße 95) and Moselglück (Balduinstraße 43) — both offer well-maintained bikes right in Zell.

accordion.title: Air conditioning
accordion.content:
Is there air conditioning in the rooms?

There is no classic air conditioning in our historic house. On particularly warm days, we're happy to bring a modern, bladeless tower fan (8 speed settings) to your room on request — just let us know.

accordion.title: Lactose, gluten, etc.
accordion.content:
Can food intolerances like lactose or gluten be accommodated at breakfast?

We may not always have every product for every intolerance in stock as standard. It's best to let us know your needs already at the time of booking — we're happy to accommodate you.

How many rooms are there in total?

We have five lovingly furnished rooms: two with a balcony (Room 1 & 2), a studio without a balcony (Room 3), a room with a view of the castle and the Moselle (Room 4), and a cozy room with charming sloped ceilings (Room 5).

How many people can stay overnight in total?

We have five double rooms, so up to ten people can stay with us at the same time.

accordion.title: Family and children
accordion.content:
Is Haus Till E suitable for families with children?

Haus Till E is regularly booked by entire families or groups of friends — we've had the pleasure of witnessing many a milestone birthday and hosting three or four generations at once throughout the house. It brings us great joy to provide the setting for unforgettable shared moments.

accordion.title: Arrival and departure times
accordion.content:
When is check-in and check-out?

Since we run the hotel with a small team, check-in is available between 4:00 PM and 6:00 PM. If your room happens to be ready earlier, we'll be sure to let you know right away. We wish we could just wave a magic wand – until that works out, we simply work quickly and carefully so your room is ready by 4:00 PM.

We would ask you to check out by 11.00 am.

text: Each of our five rooms is lovingly and uniquely furnished for you. On the second floor, two rooms with their own balcony await you (Rooms 1 & 2), as well as a spacious studio without a balcony (Room 3). On the third floor you'll find a large room with a wonderful view of the castle and the Moselle (Room 4) and a cosy room with charming sloped ceilings (Room 5).

Antique small furniture pieces, original Art Deco ball lamps and real plants create an atmospheric ambience in your rooms — complemented by exclusive artworks that an international artist created especially for each room. 'The rooms combine the luxury of the 1920s with all the comforts of the present' — that's how a guest described it recently. A description we're very fond of.
Please note: our house has no lift — the rooms are only accessible via the stairs.

hosts.eyebrow: 03 — Your hosts look forward to welcoming you
text: We are Jan and René — and Haus Till E is our passion project. The house has been around for many decades. When we first stepped inside in April 2022, it was all over for us: we fell in love on the spot with this beautiful Art Deco property — with its authentic stained glass, the old wooden staircase, and the idyllic garden that Jan has lovingly tended ever since.

We moved from Berlin to the Moselle to find exactly what makes Zell so special: peace and quiet, clean air, wide and hilly nature, warm-hearted people, and the occasional sip of good Moselle wine. We want to share this love at first sight with you and get you excited about this wonderful building from the 1920s. That's why we warmly invite you to be our guests.
Finally, we'd like to share a few details with you that accompany and inspire us and life at Haus Till E.

Rosa.text:
MAKING LIGHT TANGIBLE - ROSA M HESSLING 

We first met Rosa M Hessling at our very first Christmas market in the garden of Haus Till E — and it clicked instantly. We've been proud to display her work with us ever since. 

Rosa was born in Zell an der Mosel, the very same town where our hotel is located. She studied at the Düsseldorf Art Academy under Prof. Christian Megert and Prof. Nam June Paik. Alongside numerous solo and group exhibitions across Europe, her work has been shown over the past four decades in, among other places, Australia, the USA and South Africa. Today, Rosa is an artist whose works are represented in numerous renowned public and private collections — while remaining deeply connected to her roots on the Moselle. 

Using sophisticated techniques and a wide variety of materials, she explores how light refracts and reflects, so that her works always appear different depending on the viewer’s perspective and the angle of the light 

For us, this is more than wall decoration: our guests experience the art of an artist who comes from the very same Moselle valley in which they spend their stay — and who is at the same time internationally celebrated.

Bjorn.text:
SOCIAL CRITIQUE MADE VISIBLE - BJØRN WIINBLAD 

We discovered Bjørn Wiinblad through Rosenthal porcelain — rather by chance, yet with great consequences. On the day we bought the hotel, it was Jan's birthday, and René was looking for a gift with a connection to Till Eulenspiegel. In doing so, he came across Bjørn's porcelain — and what began as a gift idea quickly became a passion. 

René has gathered individual selected collector's pieces to give space throughout the house to Bjørn's design and Till's stories. 

What's special about these stories: as a clever fool, Till holds up a mirror to those around him, wittily exposing the weaknesses and injustices of society. We find this very wit and this love of detail again in Bjørn's drawings: in the typical design style of the 1970s, he tells figures and stories playfully, delicately and with great attention to detail. 

Why is our house actually called 'Till E'? We'd love to tell you that story in person — when you're staying with us.

Romina.text:
PAST AND PRESENT UNITED - ROMINA RESSIA 

We became aware of Romina Ressia back in the 2010s — and her artworks have never let go of us since. The Argentine photographer draws on classical Renaissance and Baroque compositions in her portraits — formality and rigour — only to break them with unexpected everyday motifs: chewing gum, popcorn, a burger. Her work has been exhibited in London, New York and Paris, among other places; in 2017 the International Color Awards named her Photographer of the Year. 

This very connection between past and present is exactly what we wanted to create at Haus Till E, too. 

When we opened our hotel, we knew immediately: this is the perfect place for Romina's art to unfold. Because our house, too, combines Gothic-revival vaults with flat screens, Art Deco lamps with concrete tables, antique castle furniture with modern conveniences. 

This means the past doesn't become a museum here, but stays alive and relevant in the present — just like in Romina's images.

text: At Haus Till E, everything revolves around what people quietly long for: peace to arrive, time to do nothing — and, if you like, a little activity in between. From our favourite viewpoint bench (our personal 'Moselle cinema'), just a 10-minute walk from Haus Till E, you can watch life unfold on the Moselle and simply let time pass by.

If you prefer to be active, you'll find hiking trails right on the doorstep of Haus Till E, such as the Liebesschlucht (Lovers' Gorge, 11.1 km) or the Marienburg circular trail (15.2 km), relaxed cycling tours along the Moselle, or more sporty stretches up into the steep vineyards of the 'Zeller Schwarze Katz'. And as a reward, more than 20 passionate winegrowers and restaurants for every taste await you in Zell (Mosel) — from Greek to Asian, from ice cream sundaes to chocolate.

And if you look closely, you'll discover cultural hidden gems right at Haus Till E: classical concerts in the vaulted cellar, band performances in the garden, murder mystery dinners with a multi-course menu — experiences you won't find by googling, but only by staying with us.

accordion.title: Town
accordion.content: In town, we most enjoy the Moselle promenade and strolling along Balduinstraße with its small shops and cafés. And from Kaimt, on the other side of the Moselle, you get the finest view of Zell's old town — with its towers, half-timbered houses and over 2,000 years of winemaking history visible on every corner.

accordion.title: Countryside
accordion.content:
Around Zell, two very different landscapes meet: the Eifel and the Hunsrück. On one side, wide views over gentle hills; on the other, dense forests with clearings that invite you to linger.

A highlight in the Hunsrück is the Geierlay suspension bridge near Sosberg — at 360 metres long and up to 100 metres high, one of Germany's most spectacular suspension bridges and pure adrenaline for anyone who isn't afraid of heights.

accordion.title: River
accordion.content: By boat, you can travel from Zell to Cochem, Beilstein, Traben-Trarbach or Bernkastel-Kues — past castles and vineyards, almost like travelling through a model railway landscape. And since you can take your bicycles on board, you can comfortably combine one leg of the trip by boat and cycle the other, just as you please.

accordion.title: Mountains
accordion.content:
Right at the foot of Haus Till E lies the famous steep vineyard „Zeller Schwarze Katz“ — and it's here, in the heart of the vineyard, that our house stands.

Right behind Haus Till E begins the Collis circular trail (7.9 km, approx. 2 hrs 30 min, 210 m elevation gain), leading up to the Collis Tower, built in 1906, with a wonderful view over the town; Merl and Briedel also offer mountains with spectacular views.

Just a 10-minute walk from Haus Till E is our viewpoint bench, our very own 'Moselle cinema': from here you can watch the activity on the water and in the vineyards — the most beautiful and relaxing show nature has to offer.

accordion.title: Hiking
accordion.content:
Anyone wanting to experience nature on foot is in exactly the right place at Haus Till E.

The Liebesschlucht (11.1 km, moderate, approx. 3 hrs 15 min, 266 m elevation gain) leads you past the pilgrimage site of Marienhöhe through the forest down into a romantic rocky gorge.

The Marienburg circular trail (15.2 km, moderate, approx. 4 hrs 35 min, 383 m elevation gain) rewards you with a detour to the Prinzenkopf Tower and grand panoramic views of Germany's tightest Moselle bend.

And the Collis circular trail (7.9 km, moderate, approx. 2 hrs 30 min, 210 m elevation gain) leads up to the historic Collis Tower with a view over Zell and the Zellerland region. Three very different routes — all within reach of Haus Till E.

accordion.title: Cycling
accordion.content:
Whether relaxed or sporty — at Haus Till E you'll find the right route.

Right along the Moselle it's flat and gently graded, ideal for a leisurely bike outing.

If you prefer something more athletic, venture up into the steep vineyards — short, sharp climbs included, rewarded with great views.

accordion.title: Wellness
accordion.content: About a 30-minute drive from Haus Till E lies the Vulkaneifel Therme in Bad Bertrich — Germany's only Glauber's salt thermal spa, with a thermal pool, six saunas and a wide range of wellness treatments. A perfect outing if you're longing for water, warmth and a bit of pampering.

accordion.title: Enjoying wine
accordion.content:
More than 20 winegrowers shape our Zell region with passion, professionalism and skill — producing excellent, multiple award-winning wines. In the steep vineyards, grapes are harvested by hand, with a love for the product you can taste when sampling it. Our winemakers set trends, and the younger generation boldly tries new things.

In numerous wine taverns and vinotheques you can sample, taste and, of course, take the wines home with you.

accordion.title: Enjoying food
accordion.content:
There's something for every taste: Greek at 'El Grego', Italian at 'Giovanni', Indian at 'La Terrazza', German at Hotel 'Zum Grünen Kranz', and Asian with top-notch sushi at 'Koi' — all restaurants that have convinced with great quality for years.

The best ice cream sundaes in town can be found at 'Stülb', 'Venezia' or 'Perilli', the tastiest cakes at 'Stadtcafé Stülb' — and if you're after a sweet treat, you'll find it at 'DaKo', our Belgian chocolatier.

accordion.title: Enjoying culture
accordion.content:
In the summer months, 'Summer in the City' awaits you — Thursday evenings with laid-back live music at changing locations in Zell, sometimes at a winery, sometimes right at Haus Till E in the garden.

From autumn to spring, we're drawn to the KulturKino Kaimt with its lovingly curated film programme. And in between, there are always small concerts at Haus Till E or with friends — in the garden, in the living room or in the vaulted cellar, ranging from classical guitar to big band to minimalist electronic beats, plus murder mystery dinners with a multi-course menu.

You'll find the current dates on our events page.

items.title: How far is the viewpoint bench from Haus Till E?

items.title: Which hiking trails start near Haus Till E?
items.content: Right at the doorstep of Haus Till E begin the Collis circular trail (7.9 km), the Liebesschlucht (11.1 km) and the Marienburg circular trail (15.2 km).

items.title: How long and how difficult is the Marienburg circular trail?
items.content: The Marienburg circular trail is 15.2 km long, of moderate difficulty, and takes about 4 hours 35 minutes with 383 m of elevation gain.

items.title: Where is Haus Till E located?
items.content: Haus Till E is located at the foot of the steep vineyard 'Zeller Schwarze Katz' in Zell (Mosel), directly on the Moselle.

items.title: How far is the Vulkaneifel Therme in Bad Bertrich?
items.content: The Vulkaneifel Therme in Bad Bertrich is about a 30-minute drive from Haus Till E.

items.title: How long is the Geierlay suspension bridge?
items.content: The Geierlay suspension bridge in the Hunsrück is 360 metres long and reaches up to 100 metres above the valley between Sosberg and Mörsdorf.

items.title: Federweisser Festival - hosted by MOS:L WEIN:EVENTS
items.description: The Zell marketplace turns into four days full of indulgence, music and togetherness at the Federweisser Festival – with Federweisser, great food, a wonderful program for young and old, and plenty of good cheer, Zell looks forward to welcoming you! MOS:L WEIN:EVENTS is hosting this lovely event and Haus Till E will also be providing catering, among other things.

items.title: Zell Town & Alley Flea Market
items.location: across the whole town / Garden at Haus Till E
items.description: On October 17 and 18, the Autumn Magic in Zell invites you to browse and discover – whether it's the town and alley flea market, a children's flea market, a special shopping Sunday, or delicious autumn treats, everyone is sure to find their own little bargain and enjoy cozy autumn days in Zell! And of course there's plenty to browse in the garden at Haus Till E too – we're joining in with our friends!

image.alt: Autumn Magic Flea Market in Zell

items.title: Dekadenzia 2026 – Theme Party
items.description: The Roaring Twenties are back – for one night – at the Zell Castle Cellar with a live band, burlesque show, dance lesson, gambling den and cocktails. And the two of us are dressing up too – becoming part of the wonderful bar team for the night.

image.alt: Dekadenzia Theme Party at the Zell Castle Cellar

items.title: Advent Magic 2026
items.location: Lights Garden at Haus Till E
items.description: At the Advent Magic in Haus Till E you can look forward to cozy togetherness in the festively decorated garden, food and drink with hot mulled wine, and concerts for young and old, plus a gift cabinet full of ideas for what to give. We look forward to seeing you!

image.alt: Advent Magic in the Lights Garden

items.title: Concert at Advent Magic – 2nd Sunday of Advent
items.location: Lights Garden at Haus Till E
items.description: Rock vibes guaranteed: Friday's Five bring their infectious rock covers to the stage in a brand-new lineup! Their sound is honest, powerful, good old-fashioned rock — played with real passion. Yet despite all that rock power, they create a cozy, living-room atmosphere that gets everyone singing along and having a great time!

items.title: Concert at Advent Magic – 3rd Sunday of Advent
items.location: Lights Garden at Haus Till E
items.description: For several years now, Tobi Goldschmidt has been captivating audiences as a solo artist — and he's sure to do the same here! In his performances, original songs meet well-known hits, all reimagined in his own unmistakable style. An evening of music full of personal sound and familiar melodies given a fresh new twist!

items.title: Concert at Advent Magic – 4th Sunday of Advent
items.location: Lights Garden at Haus Till E
items.description: Get ready for a musical evening with Elias Beuren! The guitarist from the Moselle region enchants with handmade, acoustic cover music, creating a relaxed and cozy atmosphere perfect for listening and unwinding. Having grown up along the Moselle, he's become a familiar face at concerts and events in Zell — an evening of music with genuine local charm and heart!

items.title: Fairy Tale Parade of the Town of Zell
items.location: across the whole town / Garden at Haus Till E
items.description: For the first Sunday of Advent, Zell transforms into an enchanting fairy-tale town: the Zell Business Association invites you to the grand fairy-tale parade through the festively decorated old town. Starting at 5:30 pm, well-known fairy-tale characters such as Mother Hulda, the Nutcracker and Snow White parade through the streets, delighting young and old alike. Starting at 1:00 pm, you can already browse the Advent market around the marketplace and in the town hall – featuring a lovely selection of festive decorations, handicrafts and handmade gifts. A magical start to the Advent season for the whole family!

image.alt: Fairy Tale Parade through Zell's Old Town

items.title: Music Canteen May
items.description: Look forward to a special concert highlight: Joe's Truck Stop brings genuine Americana vibes to the stage with an infectious mix of bluegrass, honky tonk and western swing. Joe's songs tell stories of life on the road, of love and heartbreak – backed by banjo, fiddle and plenty of joy for playing. A concert evening guaranteed to deliver good spirits and wanderlust feelings!

image.alt: Garden concert at Haus Till E

items.title: Music Canteen June
items.description: Sean K. Preston, an internationally touring artist from Baltimore, brings gritty honky-tonk, dirty blues and heart-wrenching country ballads to the stage. With a raw, soulful voice, he tells stories of love, loss and wanderlust – a concert evening full of energy and true Americana soul!

image.alt: Garden concert at Haus Till E

items.title: Summer in the City
items.description: River Soul Connection guarantees a great atmosphere with their infectious classic rock & pop sound! The cover band performs well-known hits, played straight from the heart, inviting young and old to sing along and dance. A concert evening full of good vibes and familiar melodies – there's something here for every musical taste! Of course, right here at Haus Till E!

image.alt: Garden concert at Haus Till E

items.title: Music Canteen August
items.description: It's going to be loud, it's going to be great, it's going to be big! For our morning concert at Haus Till E, we welcome Magic Rhythm, the big band of the Bad Nauheim Music School, with their infectious program of swing, latin and funk. We've never had so many musicians on our little garden stage before – a true big-band experience with full sound that you won't want to miss at this cozy morning gathering!

image.alt: Garden concert at Haus Till E

items.title: Music Canteen November
items.description: The Turkey Buzzards bring genuine Americana feeling to the stage! The duo, made up of Dylan Nicholson and Eric Patterson, tell stories full of simple beauty in their songs – sometimes shaped by the sticky humidity of the Carolinas, sometimes by the dusty, dry cellars of the American West. Gritty vocals meet thoughtful harmonies, creating an honest, captivating atmosphere that takes the audience on a musical journey. The duo has already shared the stage with greats like Robert Earl Keen, Dawes and White Buffalo – a true concert experience full of authenticity and stories to dive into!

image.alt: Garden concert at Haus Till E
